business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Urban Electric Cargo Bicycles and Step-Through Scooters

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-French tradition; company law and commercial law closely aligned with French and Belgian codifications, supplemented by Luxembourg statutes implemented through the notarial system)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaty network (90+ BITs, e.g., BLEU–China BIT 1984, BLEU–South Korea BIT 1974, BLEU–UAE BIT 2013)
Luxembourg–United States Income and Capital Tax Convention (signed 3 April 1996, as amended by the Protocol of 20 May 2004)
Luxembourg–People's Republic of China DTA (1994, as amended by the Protocol of 1 February 2019)
Luxembourg–France Income Tax Treaty (signed 20 March 2018, in force 2019)
EU internal market freedoms under the TFEU, plus EU-level trade and investment agreements (e.g., CETA, EU-Japan EPA) applicable to manufacturing and exports

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Art. 180-1 et seq. of the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (SARL); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (AML/CFT Law, as amended); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law, as amended by the Law of 18 December 2020 and implementing rules of 14 March 2023); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Trade and Companies Register and company filings; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02 on AML/CFT professional obligations (as amended); FATF Recommendations as applied by the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) Luxembourg.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (post-constitutional-ruling regime: general public access removed by the Luxembourg Constitutional Court judgment No. 152 of 7 November 2022; access restricted to competent authorities, AML/CFT obliged entities performing customer due diligence, and registered 'legitimate interest' applicants under the RBE Law)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / registration extract of each corporate shareholder (Certificat d'immatriculation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent authority of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for signatory countries; Consular Legalization by the competent Luxembourg embassy/consulate for non-Hague countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (Pouvoir) granting authority to the Luxembourg incorporation notary and local counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate shareholder's board or shareholder-notarized resolution in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copies of passports or national ID for each shareholder (natural persons), gérant/director, and every UBO at or above 25%
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/ID issuing authority; copies certified by a local notary or embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation (attestation bancaire) for each contributor to the minimum share capital
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank of the contributing party
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization; independent verification by the Luxembourg receiving bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn translation into French of the corporate shareholder's articles of association and board resolutions
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator accredited in Luxembourg or a court-approved translator of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication by the translator's professional body combined with Hague Apostille / Consular Legalization where the underlying document is foreign

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all shareholders, gérants/directors, UBOs at or above 25%, and authorized signatories against (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (ii) UN Security Council sanctions, (iii) OFAC SDN/SSI lists (required for USD-denominated SWIFT TT and LC payment rails), (iv) the UK HMT sanctions list, and (v) the Luxembourg CSSF/FIU watch lists and public registry of defaulting entities. PEP identification and verification must follow FATF and 4AMLD/5AMLD standards, including capture of family members and close associates, with enhanced due diligence triggered for PEP status, high-risk countries, complex source-of-wealth structures, or mismatch between economic activity and payment rails. All CDD/EDD records must be kept for five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) online portal: https://www.lbr.lu (free availability search and e-filing interface; name clearance is initiated via a notary or directly through LBR for pre-screening)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin script; the mandatory legal form suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' must appear in the name or directly accompany it; French is the standard drafting and filing language; non-Latin characters must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet with a sworn translation filed; the name must not be misleading, contrary to public policy, or create confusion with existing RCS entries (Art. 7 of the Law of 19 December 2002)
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Bank, BCL (requires CSSF banking licence)
SICAV, SICAF, FCP, Fonds d'investissement (requires CSSF fund authorization)
PFS (Professional of the Financial Sector) (requires CSSF licence)
État, Gouvernement, Ville de Luxembourg, administrator expressions implying state or municipal patronage
Chambre de Commerce (statutorily reserved to the official Chamber)
Université, Lycée (requires Ministry of Education authorization)
Euro, Banque Centrale Européenne and any name implying EU institutional sponsorship
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: SOP: (1) Upon an RCS name refusal, the applicant or notary obtains written reasons from the LBR search office within 5 business days. (2) A written objection for reconsideration is filed with the LBR within 15 calendar days of the refusal, attaching evidence of prior use, distinctiveness, or absence of confusion under Art. 7 of the Law of 19 December 2002. (3) If the objection is denied, the applicant may institute summary proceedings (référé) before the President of the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within 40 days of the denial, seeking a judicial order to admit the name; alternatively, a full appeal on the merits may be lodged. (4) In parallel, the applicant should submit two alternative names without prejudice and may request a renewed 60-day reservation at no additional LBR fee; a formal extension of the original reservation is not automatic and requires a further submission before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Luxembourg-registered office is mandatory (Law of 31 May 1999 on company domiciliation). Pure mailbox 'virtual offices' are legally permitted as bare domiciliation but are materially insufficient for a manufacturing micro-mobility OEM; the RCS and tax authorities require a genuine place of administration and a verifiable business address in Luxembourg. Banks and the incorporating notary impose strict CDD rules on domiciliation agreements, and a pure virtual mailbox paired with production located entirely abroad will trigger substantive substance review, potential VAT reclassification, and AML enhanced due diligence. Recommended practice: valid domiciliation agreement plus a real Luxembourg/EU operating site, local payroll and management control.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 30% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by RCS/LBR, the social security authority (CCSS), or the Luxembourg tax administration within the first 36 months for an active manufacturing company; the likelihood rises above 60% where the registered office is a pure virtual mailbox and no physical operations, inventory, or employees are present in Luxembourg.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent law firm (avocat à la Cour) admitted in Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a low-risk manufacturing SARL formation with a corporate shareholder

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per document; estimated EUR 150–300 per corporate document set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization processing fees for up to five foreign public documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication fee fixed by the Law of 19 December 2002 and LBR tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RBE declaration fee per the applicable LBR fee schedule

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Part XI (Société à Responsabilité Limitée), Articles 710-1 et seq.; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers and the Register of Commerce and Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized constitutional deed (acte constitutif) containing the Articles of Association, filed with the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL must maintain a minimum subscribed share capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution; the bank's blocking certificate is delivered to the notary and the funds are released only after RCS registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, as the first management resolution of the Luxembourg SARL, that the corporate name be [Name] SARL, the registered office be fixed at [Address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and that the share capital of EUR 12,000 be fully subscribed and paid up as stated in the notarized Articles of Association. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] is appointed sole manager (gérant) with authority to execute the incorporation deed, open and operate bank accounts, make all RCS, VAT, social-security, and beneficial-ownership filings, and adopt internal governance rules. RESOLVED FURTHER that any preliminary steps already taken are ratified and that the manager may complete all statutory formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Drafting of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Guichet.lu electronic portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed corporate name to the RCS pre-validation procedure through the notary or directly via Guichet.lu. Obtain a negative certificate confirming name availability. Draft the Articles of Association in accordance with the Law of 10 August 1915, including corporate object, registered office, capital structure, and management powers.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each founding shareholder and manager
Proof of residential address for each individual officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or the articles contain deficiencies, amend the draft and resubmit through the notary. A supplementary correcting deed may be executed before the same notary if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Account and Deposit of Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution selected by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the company in formation at a Luxembourg bank. Deposit the full EUR 12,000 minimum capital and any agreed share premium. Request a bank blocking certificate confirming that the funds are irrevocably blocked for the benefit of the future company and will be remitted to the company upon RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Valid identity documents of shareholders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests supplementary KYC information or disputes the account title, correct the documentation and resubmit. A new blocking certificate must be obtained if account details change before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Constitutional Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (public notary admitted in the Grand Duchy)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the Luxembourg notary together with the subscribers and the appointed manager. The notary verifies the legality of the Articles, the capital payment certificate, the identities of the parties, and the manager's acceptance. The constitutional deed is signed, including the adoption of the registered office and the appointment of the manager, and the notary files the deed for RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all shareholders, managers, and notary signatories
Written acceptance of office by the appointed manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal or documentary defects, execute a correcting deed or provide the missing evidence before signing. Recalendar the notarial appointment if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Register of Commerce and Companies and Acquisition of Legal Personality
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS through the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary electronically transmits the constitutional deed and RCS filing forms. The RCS reviews the application, allocates the RCS registration number and Luxembourg business number, and publishes the incorporation in the electronic Compendium (RESA). Legal personality is acquired on the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Filing fee receipt issued by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query or requests clarification, the notary submits a corrective filing within 15 business days. The registration fee is not forfeited unless the application is finally rejected and a new filing is needed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Guichet.lu, Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), Administration de l'enregistrement et des domaines (AED)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, register the ultimate beneficial owners in the national beneficial ownership register (RBE) within statutory deadlines, obtain the VAT number for taxable activities, enroll the company and the manager with the social security body, and open the employer/establishment file. The manager should obtain the extracts and certificates required for the industrial licensing stage.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the constitutional deed
VAT form and business activity declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If filings are rejected, correct the forms and refile immediately. Late filings may incur administrative fines; an explanatory note and voluntary regularisation are submitted to the competent authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) and Administration de l'environnement through Guichet.lu
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment permit) and autorisation d'exploitation for a classified establishment (établissement classé)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Protection Agency), Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 classified establishment — simplified environmental registration; a full EIA report is not required for sub-threshold electric cargo bicycle assembly, coating, and battery integration, but environmental permit conditions apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with EU Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU BAT conclusions for surface treatment, Grand-Ducal VOC solvent-emissions limits for coating operations, wastewater discharge limits of COD ≤ 125 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, TSS ≤ 35 mg/L, pH 6–9.5, and hazardous-waste handling for lithium batteries, paint sludge, and used solvents under Luxembourg waste legislation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS), structural load inspection and building occupancy approval from the municipal building authority, and workplace safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD – Direct Tax Administration), 33 rue de la Gasperich, L-1615 Luxembourg, official portal: guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu; VAT competence rests with the Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT – Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Administration), with electronic filing through the eTVA module of the single official portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 – Incorporate the SARL before the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS Luxembourg) via the e-business platform (LBR.LU); upon incorporation the company is entered in the Luxembourg Central Register of Companies and automatically obtains the national Tax Identification Number (matricule national). Step 2 – The AEDT automatically issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number (n° TVA; format 'LU' followed by 8 digits) for the newly incorporated resident company; no separate registration application is required for resident entities. Step 3 – A non-resident entity that carries out taxable supplies in Luxembourg without a local establishment must actively register for VAT before the AEDT registration department through the eTVA/MyGuichet.lu portal; the application requires certified articles of association, proof of the foreign VAT/TIN registration, description of the Luxembourg taxable activity and, for non-EU applicants without an EU establishment, appointment of a Luxembourg tax representative. Step 4 – Complete the beneficial ownership declaration (RBE register) and, if the SARL operates a commercial establishment in Luxembourg, obtain the autorisation d'établissement from the Ministry of the Economy. Filing obligations start as of the registration date: VAT returns (monthly or quarterly depending on turnover), VIES/EC Sales Lists, and SAF-T accounting data filed through the electronic channels; no tax registration fee applies for standard VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a 'check-the-box' or S-corporation-style pass-through election; classification follows the legal form of the SARL (a capital company) mandatorily subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax. Elections available: (1) Fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR – 95%-or-more owned Luxembourg-resident companies and certain EEA-company permanent establishments may elect to file on a consolidated taxable-result basis for corporate income tax and municipal business tax; the election must be supported by a written application filed with the ACD. (2) VAT group election (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law for Luxembourg-established and financially integrated persons. (3) EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) and Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) elections for intra-Community distance sales and import consignments, replacing local Luxembourg registration for those flows. (4) No hybrid-mismatch elections: rules implementing EU ATAD (Law of 21 December 2017) neutralize hybrid financial instruments and hybrid entities through mandatory multilateral adjustments rather than taxpayer elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA – Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Mehrwertsteuer) imposed by the Loi modifiée du 12 février 1979 relative à la TVA, implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover (exclusive of VAT) for the small-enterprise exemption threshold (Article 25b of the Luxembourg VAT Law), above which VAT registration becomes mandatory for locally established persons; EUR 10,000 Union-wide turnover for intra-Community distance-selling/OSS registration; non-established foreign suppliers have no de minimis threshold – any taxable supply of goods or services deemed made in Luxembourg triggers immediate VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory crypto-stamping and no per-invoice API transmission to the tax administration (model differs from Italy's SdI). Mandatory PEPPOL-BIS electronic invoicing applies to B2G supplies to the Luxembourg central public administration since 1 March 2021. B2B and B2C e-invoicing remain voluntary, provided authenticity and readability requirements are met. Reporting obligations are periodic: VAT returns and EC Sales Lists (VIES) filed electronically through eTVA/MyGuichet.lu; annual SAF-T (Standard Audit File for Tax) in XML format; and forward-looking implementation of EU ViDA/European Single Reporting (ESR) for transaction-level disclosure of intra-EU cross-border supplies, effective from calendar-year 2024/2025 reporting windows.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The supply qualifies for the 0% VAT rate when goods are exported by the seller or on its behalf to a destination outside the European Union (Article 41 Luxembourg VAT Law; Article 146 Directive 2006/112/EC). Conditions: (i) physical departure of goods from EU territory, normally evidenced within 90 days of the supply; (ii) the export declaration is made in the name of the exporter/seller; (iii) the supplier receives concurrent documentary proof of the customs export procedure (MRN/ECS data) and international transport contract; (iv) for goods sold on ex-works, FOB, CIF or DDP terms, title and risk transfer must be verifiable; (v) export-related ancillary services (freight, handling, insurance, inspection) attached to exported goods may be zero-rated under Article 146(1)(c) of the VAT Directive, and offshore B2B services supplied to non-EU taxable customers are outside Luxembourg VAT scope (place-of-supply rules) and therefore effectively 0% if the recipient has no Luxembourg establishment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DAU) accepted by the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration (Administration des douanes et accises) through the ECS/ECS2 electronic export system, including the MRN and release-for-export date
Bill of Lading (ocean), CMR/CIM waybill (road/rail) or Air Waybill (air) evidencing physical dispatch of goods to a non-EU destination, with consignee name and port or airport of unloading
Commercial invoice, purchase order and payment terms evidencing the economic ownership transfer, including Incoterms and export contract documentation
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 / bank payment confirmation evidencing the actual receipt and ultimate repatriation of export proceeds in convertible currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg Customs and the AEDT may audit zero-rating claims at any time within the ordinary 5-year reassessment period (extended to 10 years in cases of fraud). If the documentary chain (customs MRN, transport title, remittance evidence) is incomplete or inconsistent, export zero-rating is withdrawn, the supply is recharacterized as domestic, output VAT is clawed back at 17% and statutory late-payment interest accrues from the original due date. Fraudulent export zero-rating – including forged transport documents, circular export/import transactions or carousel VAT fraud – additionally triggers administrative fines of up to double the tax evaded (capped at EUR 250,000), criminal prosecution under the Luxembourg tax fraud law (Law of 23 March 2016) with custodial sentences up to 5 years (up to 10 years for organized fraud), retroactive denial of input VAT deductions, joint and several liability of directors and tax representatives, and publication of the sanction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem; monetary policy and foreign-exchange policy competence are vested in the European Central Bank (ECB), while the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises banking conduct, AML compliance and payment institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility. Luxembourg is a Eurozone member state and imposes no exchange-control regime; Article 63 TFEU guarantees the free movement of capital and payments, and both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully liberalized. Profit remittance is subject to the standard 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax, but an EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption (10% shareholding, minimum 12-month holding period) removes withholding for qualifying EU corporate shareholders, and treaty relief applies for non-EU shareholders. There are no administrative approvals, currency allocation queues or repatriation ceilings; the SARL may freely invoice in EUR, USD, CNH or any convertible currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory repatriation timeline, no mandatory bank-account concentration requirement, and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in domestic or offshore accounts in any currency; however, the BCL balance-of-payments statistical regime requires the resident credit institution to report each transaction above the reporting threshold (set at or near EUR 12,500) and to identify the underlying economic-purpose code, so the SARL must tag all cross-border wires with accurate purpose labels to avoid BCL data-quality queries.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte de blocage) and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and blocked capital deposit
Operational Account, trade-finance and documentary credit line
Operational Account, multi-currency account and LC services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium feasibility. A CSSF-authorised or EEA-passported electronic-money institution (EMI) under PSD2 may hold minor operational float, but it cannot issue the statutory blocked-funds certificate (attestation de blocage) required for SARL share-capital deposit, and major Luxembourg banks will not accept an offshore digital EMI as maintainer of the capital escrow or as primary settlement bank. For trade disbursements above EUR 50,000 and documentary LC workflows, the EMI rail is legally constrained by its absence of a full credit-institution licence and by correspondent-bank de-risking policies; therefore, an offline regulated credit institution remains mandatory for the SARL's anchor treasury relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid, weighted toward physical attendance. Since the CSSF digital-onboarding guidance of 2020, remote video-KYC is possible for low-risk profiles, but a newly incorporated manufacturing SARL with Asian supply-chain payment flows is ordinarily classified as standard-risk, requiring at least one authorised manager/director to attend a physical or notarised interview at the bank (or before a Luxembourg notary) for identity verification and signature-mandate confirmation. Non-appearing directors must execute a notarised and apostilled power of attorney specifically covering banking onboarding, and the bank will request certified passport copies, proof of address, UBO declarations and the RBE extract; full remote opening is accepted only by a minority of banks and is conditioned on all signatories passing video identification and none being a politically exposed person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial share-capital deposit funded by a third-party loan rather than the shareholder's own funds, activating source-of-funds (SoF) review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised shareholder loan agreement; 12 months of bank statements on the lender's account evidencing economic capacity; passport and tax-residency certificates of lender and borrowing SARL; written confirmation that no cash collateral, receivable financing or virtual-asset proceeds were used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner holding through a multi-layered non-EU structure or a FATF follow-up jurisdiction, triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) extract identifying the natural person at each layer; corporate-chain chart with registry numbers for all intermediate entities; source-of-wealth documentation (sale agreements, dividend resolutions, liquidation distributions); negative-media screening report; CSSF-compliant beneficial-ownership declaration executed by all directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SARL with high projected outbound payment velocity to China/Taiwan for e-bike component imports before credit history is established.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with audited 24-month cash-flow projections; proforma supplier invoices and master supply agreements; freight-forwarder contracts; end-use declarations for lithium-ion battery and controller imports; incoterms matrix and customs HS classification sheets (HS 8711.60 / 8711.90); Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce trade-reference letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recent RCS registration (less than six months) and a broad 'electric mobility' activity description raising ESG and reputational-screening concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) abstract reflecting NACE/ISIC 3091; website and product catalogue evidencing physical OEM operations; lease agreement for production premises; Luxembourg VAT (TVA) registration certificate; purchase orders from EU distributors; product-liability insurance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Any crypto-asset adjacency, including shareholder funding sourced from crypto exchanges or invoices referencing digital-asset settlement, triggering the bank's model-risk committee block.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed governance rider confirming zero acceptance of virtual currencies for corporate receivables; bank statements evidencing fiat-only inflows; compliance self-assessment mapping all goods to ISIC 3091 and HS 8711.60; denial-of-crypto-association letter executed by the managing director; sanctions-screening clearance reports for every counterparty.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The SARL's statutory share capital must be wired by SEPA Credit Transfer or SWIFT MT103 in EUR to the Luxembourg bank's blocked account (compte de blocage) before notarial execution; the bank issues the blocked-funds certificate (attestation de blocage) required by the Luxembourg notary, with funds released to the operational account only upon RCS registration. The remittance instruction should state the SARL's corporate name, the notarial deed reference and the BCL balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment in equity capital; no prior administrative or central-bank approval is required, and no FX conversion is needed because the investment is made in EUR from the shareholder's own account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Three primary clearing rails: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR for EU suppliers, freight forwarders, customs and payroll, with day-ahead value dating; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for high-value TT wires in USD, EUR or CNH to Asian component suppliers, supported by invoice-backed payment instructions carrying full beneficiary-bank and SWIFT/BIC details, and automatically reported by the Luxembourg bank to BCL balance-of-payments statistics above the EUR 12,500 threshold; and (iii) irrevocable documentary letters of credit governed by UCP600 and ISBP745 for containerised component batches, issued by the Luxembourg issuing bank and advised or confirmed by a beneficiary-side bank in the supplier's jurisdiction. The ERP payment file must embed the ISIC 3091 activity reference and order numbers in the structured remittance field to accelerate customs clearance, reconciliation and BCL statistical classification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY and EUR/CNH) traded bilaterally with a Luxembourg credit institution under ISDA documentation, limited to underlying import and export trade-flow hedging; the SARL, as an EMIR non-financial counterparty below the clearing threshold (NFC-), is exempt from central clearing for FX forwards and only reports to a trade repository.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing USD/CNH for offshore renminbi exposure conversion into EUR, executed to hedge supplier payments invoiced in CNY where domestic deliverability is unavailable; subject to the same NFC- EMIR reporting-only treatment.

FX swaps (spot-forward swap combinations between EUR, USD and CNH) for short-term liquidity and disbursement-date alignment, with physically settled leg obligations and no mandatory variation-margin posting under EMIR exemptions for physically settled FX forwards.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNY) used to swap the currency basis of ancillary term-loan liabilities against forecast USD and CNH revenue flows from North American and Asian distributors, structured under a Luxembourg-law-governed ISDA/CSA and executed bilaterally as an NFC-.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts filing (comptes annuels) with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' approval of annual accounts within 6 months of the financial year-end; deposit with the RCS within 1 month of approval, i.e., no later than 31 July for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal default notice (mise en demeure) from the RCS; on petition of any interested party or the Public Prosecutor, the district court may order filing under a coercive penalty payment; criminal fine of EUR 100 to EUR 5,000; persistent non-filing over three years triggers compulsory judicial winding-up and administrative strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the beneficial owners register (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE) operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 1 month following the anniversary of the company's registration date in the RBE; any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 1 month of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines of EUR 100 to EUR 250,000 for the SARL and its managers for non-filing, late filing, or inaccurate UBO data; the court may also order publicity of the infringement in the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax and municipal business tax return (Form 400)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Inland Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 May following the tax year for a 31 December year-end; electronic filing extensions are available; for non-calendar accounting periods the deadline is the last day of the fifth month following the accounting year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of EUR 100 to EUR 500; default interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; 10% surcharge for negligence; criminal sanctions for intentional evasion

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required when the SARL exceeds two of the three following criteria for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, and average workforce above 50 full-time employees; shareholders holding at least 10% of the share capital may additionally request a special audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified by the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial companies and accounting, transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted by the EU is optional for unlisted SARLs but mandatory for consolidated financial statements of listed groups; accounts must be prepared in euros and follow the official chart of accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL manager must file the initial beneficial ownership declaration within 1 month of incorporation and annually confirm the accuracy of the registered data within 1 month of the anniversary of the RBE registration date. Share transfers in the SARL must be declared online within 1 month of each change to keep the beneficial ownership register aligned; confirmation is executed by a natural-person signatory, typically the manager or an authorized director, and covers all individuals holding more than 25% of capital, voting rights, or equivalent control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
